Square image of ONE object for 3D modelling: a tall temple spire built long ago by ants from packed clay, about three times as tall as it is wide, tapering to a blunt tip. A narrow spiral ramp winds up around it from the base to the tip in three turns, a ledge with tiny steps; the ramp's outer edge is inlaid with a thin continuous line of pale bone-white clay, so the path reads clearly all the way up. The body is built of stacked courses of terracotta clay, each course slightly bulging, with fine horizontal layer lines; four or five small round windows open along the ramp, dark inside; a short carved groove like an ant trail runs beside each window. Weathered: edges a little chipped, a few hairline cracks, a few crumbs of clay at the foot. Terracotta red, rust and ochre clay; the inlay pale bone. Three-quarter view from slightly above, the whole object fully visible and centred with margin. Realistic and finely crafted, like a detailed museum miniature: crisp forms and a clear structure; the detail sits in the paths, openings and layer lines, the large surfaces stay calm. Even, soft studio light, no strong shadows. Background: one perfectly flat, uniform very light neutral grey (#E8ECEC). Avoid: text, labels, frame, ground plane, cast shadow, glow, glitter, sparkles, noisy micro-texture, extra objects, plants, moss, ants.
